ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, CD is a chord, and CD $\perp$ AB at point E. Connect DO and extend it to intersect $\odot O$ at point F. Connect AF, which intersects CD at point G, with CG = AG, and connect AC. AC $\parallel$ DF; if AB = 12, what are the lengths of AC and GD?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect CO,\\
since AB$\perp$CD,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AC} $= $\overset{\frown}{AD}$, CE=DE,\\
since $\angle$DCA=$\angle$CAF,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AD} $= $\overset{\frown}{CF}$,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AC} $= $\overset{\frown}{AD} $= $\overset{\frown}{CF}$,\\
thus $\angle$AOD=$\angle$AOC=$\angle$COF,\\
since DF is the diameter,\\
thus $\angle$AOD=$\angle$AOC=$\angle$COF=$60^\circ$,\\
since OA=OC,\\
thus $\triangle$AOC is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus AC=AO=6, $\angle$CAO=$60^\circ$,\\
since CE$\perp$AO,\\
thus AE=EO=3, $\angle$ACD=$30^\circ$,\\
thus CE=3$\sqrt{3}$=DE,\\
since AG$^{2}$=GE$^{2}$+AE$^{2}$,\\
thus AG$^{2}$=（3$\sqrt{3}$−AG）$^{2}$+9,\\
thus AG=2$\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus GE=$\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus DG=4$\sqrt{3}$.\\
Therefore, the lengths of AC and GD are respectively AC=\boxed{6} and DG=\boxed{4\sqrt{3}}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the center of the circle is O, AB is a horizontal diameter, A is at the left endpoint and B is at the right endpoint; CD is a vertical chord on the left side, perpendicular to AB and intersecting it at E, with C above and D below; D, O, F are collinear, and after DO is extended, it intersects the circle at F in the upper right; AF connects A to F and intersects the vertical chord CD at G, and G is located between C and E; AC is also connected in the figure, and AC is parallel to DF. Then reason: AB=12, so the radius of the circle OA=OC=OD=OF=6. Connect CO. Because the diameter AB passes through the center of the circle and is perpendicular to the chord CD, it bisects the chord CD, giving CE=DE, and C and D are symmetric with respect to AB, so arc AC=arc AD. Also because G is on CD, G is on AF, and CG=AG, triangle ACG is an isosceles triangle, ∠DCA=∠GCA=∠CAG=∠CAF. The arcs subtended by two equal inscribed angles are equal, so arc AD=arc CF. Therefore arc AC=arc AD=arc CF. Since D, O, F are collinear, DF is a diameter, so the semicircular arc from D to F is divided into three equal parts by arc DA, arc AC, and arc CF, and the central angle corresponding to each part is 60°, namely ∠AOD=∠AOC=∠COF=60°. In triangle AOC, OA=OC=6 and ∠AOC=60°, so triangle AOC is an equilateral triangle, hence AC=6. Because CE is perpendicular to AO, and triangle AOC is an equilateral triangle, E is the midpoint of AO, AE=EO=3, CE=3√3. Also CE=DE, so DE=3√3. Let GE=t, then CG=CE-GE=3√3-t. In right triangle AGE, AG^2=AE^2+GE^2=9+t^2; also AG=CG=3√3-t, so 9+t^2=(3√3-t)^2, solving gives t=√3. Therefore GD=GE+DE=√3+3√3=4√3.

method.method_draft: Synthetic arc/angle route. From the image, first note the layout: AB is the horizontal diameter with center O, CD is the vertical chord meeting AB at E on the left of O, C is above D, DO continues through O to F on the upper-right arc, AF crosses CD at G, and AC is drawn parallel to DF. From the text, use AB=12, so OA=OC=OD=OF=6; CD ⟂ AB; CG=AG; AC ∥ DF. Draw CO. Since the diameter AB through O is perpendicular to chord CD, it bisects the chord and the corresponding arcs, so CE=DE and arc AC equals arc AD. Because AC ∥ DF, relate the inscribed angles to get ∠DCA=∠CAF, hence the intercepted arcs AD and CF are equal. Therefore arcs AC, AD, and CF are equal. Since D,O,F are collinear, DF is a diameter, so the semicircle from D to F through A,C is split into three equal arcs, each giving a 60° central angle. Thus ∠AOC=60°, and triangle AOC is equilateral, giving AC=6. Then in the equilateral triangle with CE perpendicular to AO, get AE=EO=3 and CE=DE=3√3. Finally, from the image G lies on CD between C and E; set GE=t. In right triangle AGE, AG^2=AE^2+GE^2, while CG=CE-GE=3√3-t and CG=AG. Solve sqrt(9+t^2)=3√3-t to get t=√3, then GD=GE+DE=√3+3√3=4√3.

先描述图像：图中圆心为 O，AB 是水平直径，A 在左端、B 在右端；CD 是靠左的一条竖直弦，与 AB 垂直交于 E，C 在上、D 在下；D、O、F 共线，DO 延长后交圆于右上方的 F；AF 从 A 连到 F，并与竖直弦 CD 交于 G，且 G 位于 C 与 E 之间；图中还连接了 AC，并且 AC 与 DF 平行。
再推理：AB=12，所以圆的半径 OA=OC=OD=OF=6。连接 CO。因为直径 AB 过圆心且垂直于弦 CD，所以它平分弦 CD，得到 CE=DE，并且 C、D 关于 AB 对称，因此弧 AC=弧 AD。又因为 G 在 CD 上、G 在 AF 上，且 CG=AG，所以三角形 ACG 为等腰三角形，∠DCA=∠GCA=∠CAG=∠CAF。两个相等的圆周角所对的弧相等，因此弧 AD=弧 CF。于是弧 AC=弧 AD=弧 CF。由于 D、O、F 共线，DF 是直径，所以从 D 到 F 的半圆弧被弧 DA、弧 AC、弧 CF 分成三等份，每份对应的圆心角都是 60°，即 ∠AOD=∠AOC=∠COF=60°。在三角形 AOC 中，OA=OC=6 且 ∠AOC=60°，所以三角形 AOC 是等边三角形，故 AC=6。
因为 CE 垂直 AO，且三角形 AOC 为等边三角形，所以 E 是 AO 的中点，AE=EO=3，CE=3√3。又 CE=DE，所以 DE=3√3。设 GE=t，则 CG=CE-GE=3√3-t。直角三角形 AGE 中，AG^2=AE^2+GE^2=9+t^2；又 AG=CG=3√3-t，所以 9+t^2=(3√3-t)^2，解得 t=√3。因此 GD=GE+DE=√3+3√3=4√3。

再推理：AB=12，所以圆的半径 OA=OC=OD=OF=6。连接 CO。因为直径 AB 过圆心且垂直于弦 CD，所以它平分弦 CD，得到 CE=DE，并且 C、D 关于 AB 对称，因此弧 AC=弧 AD。又因为 G 在 CD 上、G 在 AF 上，且 CG=AG，所以三角形 ACG 为等腰三角形，∠DCA=∠GCA=∠CAG=∠CAF。两个相等的圆周角所对的弧相等，因此弧 AD=弧 CF。于是弧 AC=弧 AD=弧 CF。由于 D、O、F 共线，DF 是直径，所以从 D 到 F 的半圆弧被弧 DA、弧 AC、弧 CF 分成三等份，每份对应的圆心角都是 60°，即 ∠AOD=∠AOC=∠COF=60°。在三角形 AOC 中，OA=OC=6 且 ∠AOC=60°，所以三角形 AOC 是等边三角形，故 AC=6。
因为 CE 垂直 AO，且三角形 AOC 为等边三角形，所以 E 是 AO 的中点，AE=EO=3，CE=3√3。又 CE=DE，所以 DE=3√3。设 GE=t，则 CG=CE-GE=3√3-t。直角三角形 AGE 中，AG^2=AE^2+GE^2=9+t^2；又 AG=CG=3√3-t，所以 9+t^2=(3√3-t)^2，解得 t=√3。因此 GD=GE+DE=√3+3√3=4√3。

method.method_draft: Analytic coordinate/slope route. From the image, place AB on the x-axis with O as the origin, A=(-6,0), B=(6,0). Since CD is vertical and lies left of O, write E=(-p,0), C=(-p,q), D=(-p,-q), with p,q>0. From the text AB=12, so the circle has radius 6, hence p^2+q^2=36. Because DO is extended through O to F, F is the point opposite D on the circle, so F=(p,q). Now use the text condition AC ∥ DF. The slope of AC is q/(6-p), and the slope of DF is (q-(-q))/(p-(-p))=q/p. Equating slopes gives p=3. Then p^2+q^2=36 gives q=3√3. Therefore AC=sqrt((6-p)^2+q^2)=sqrt(3^2+(3√3)^2)=6. To find GD, use the visual fact that G lies on CD between C and E, so write G=(-3,r) with 0<r<3√3. The given CG=AG gives 3√3-r=sqrt(((-3)-(-6))^2+r^2)=sqrt(9+r^2). Solving yields r=√3. Since D=(-3,-3√3), GD=r-(-3√3)=4√3.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, CD is a chord, and CD $\perp$ AB at point E. Connect DO and extend it to intersect $\odot O$ at point F. Connect AF, which intersects CD at point G, with CG = AG, and connect AC. AC $\parallel$ DF; if AB = 12, what are the lengths of AC and GD?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect CO,\\
since AB$\perp$CD,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AC} $= $\overset{\frown}{AD}$, CE=DE,\\
since $\angle$DCA=$\angle$CAF,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AD} $= $\overset{\frown}{CF}$,\\
thus $\overset{\frown}{AC} $= $\overset{\frown}{AD} $= $\overset{\frown}{CF}$,\\
thus $\angle$AOD=$\angle$AOC=$\angle$COF,\\
since DF is the diameter,\\
thus $\angle$AOD=$\angle$AOC=$\angle$COF=$60^\circ$,\\
since OA=OC,\\
thus $\triangle$AOC is an equilateral triangle,\\
thus AC=AO=6, $\angle$CAO=$60^\circ$,\\
since CE$\perp$AO,\\
thus AE=EO=3, $\angle$ACD=$30^\circ$,\\
thus CE=3$\sqrt{3}$=DE,\\
since AG$^{2}$=GE$^{2}$+AE$^{2}$,\\
thus AG$^{2}$=(3$\sqrt{3}$−AG)$^{2}$+9,\\
thus AG=2$\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus GE=$\sqrt{3}$,\\
thus DG=4$\sqrt{3}$.\\
Therefore, the lengths of AC and GD are respectively AC=\boxed{6} and DG=\boxed{4\sqrt{3}}
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the center of the circle is O, AB is a horizontal diameter, A is at the left endpoint and B is at the right endpoint; CD is a vertical chord on the left side, perpendicular to AB and intersecting it at E, with C above and D below; D, O, F are collinear, and after DO is extended, it intersects the circle at F in the upper right; AF connects A to F and intersects the vertical chord CD at G, and G is located between C and E; AC is also connected in the figure, and AC is parallel to DF.
Then reason: AB=12, so the radius of the circle OA=OC=OD=OF=6. Connect CO. Because the diameter AB passes through the center of the circle and is perpendicular to the chord CD, it bisects the chord CD, giving CE=DE, and C and D are symmetric with respect to AB, so arc AC=arc AD. Also because G is on CD, G is on AF, and CG=AG, triangle ACG is an isosceles triangle, ∠DCA=∠GCA=∠CAG=∠CAF. The arcs subtended by two equal inscribed angles are equal, so arc AD=arc CF. Therefore arc AC=arc AD=arc CF. Since D, O, F are collinear, DF is a diameter, so the semicircular arc from D to F is divided into three equal parts by arc DA, arc AC, and arc CF, and the central angle corresponding to each part is 60°, namely ∠AOD=∠AOC=∠COF=60°. In triangle AOC, OA=OC=6 and ∠AOC=60°, so triangle AOC is an equilateral triangle, hence AC=6.
Because CE is perpendicular to AO, and triangle AOC is an equilateral triangle, E is the midpoint of AO, AE=EO=3, CE=3√3. Also CE=DE, so DE=3√3. Let GE=t, then CG=CE-GE=3√3-t. In right triangle AGE, AG^2=AE^2+GE^2=9+t^2; also AG=CG=3√3-t, so 9+t^2=(3√3-t)^2, solving gives t=√3. Therefore GD=GE+DE=√3+3√3=4√3.
